transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess what made me come in is... the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling really flat and heavy lately. I just stopped initiating them. Like, I usually do these photography walks on the weekends. I have this vintage 35-millimeter camera—it was my uncle's, actually, and it has this beautiful leather strap. You just don't see craftsmanship like that anymore, you know? Everything now is just plastic and disposable. People take a thousand photos on their phones and never even print them out. 

But anyway, I haven't been taking it out. And mentoring the kids, or even just keeping a clean calendar... which is weird for me, because I'm an executive admin, so calendars are my whole life. We actually just switched to this new scheduling software at work, and the interface is just a complete disaster. The color-coding doesn't sync right with the mobile app, and my boss is always double-booking himself if I don't watch him like a hawk... but, um, wait, what was I saying? 

Right, yeah. I just haven't been doing my usual stuff. It all just feels like too much effort right now.
About how long have you been feeling this flat and heavy way?

I'd say... it's been about a year and three months now. Yeah, right around then. It all really kicked off after my family member's health and behavior started changing, and I had to step in and take on a lot more of the coordination for them. 

Because, you know, navigating the healthcare system is basically a full-time job on its own. I mean, I'm an executive admin, so I'm used to organizing things and wrangling schedules, but dealing with these insurance phone trees is just... it's completely absurd. You say "representative" and the robot voice says, "I think you said billing." And then they put you on hold, and it's always that exact same smooth jazz track. Did you know that specific hold song was actually recorded in some guy's garage in the late 80s? I read a whole article about it once. It’s called "Opus Number One." They say it's designed to lower your heart rate, but honestly, after hearing it loop for forty-five minutes while trying to fix a co-pay error, it does the exact opposite. I actually prefer silence, or maybe just some light classical music, like the cello. Cello is very grounding. My neighbor used to play the cello, actually, but then he moved to Portland... 

But, um, anyway. Yeah. About a year and three months of feeling this way.

When you have those stretches of feeling unusually upbeat or irritable, about how long do they typically last?

Well, those stretches... I'd say they've been happening on and off for about eleven months now. Yeah, these periods where I'm just so driven and confident, and I barely even need to sleep. My sister uses one for her baby, too, but hers has this little nightlight projector that puts stars on the ceiling. I think it's a bit much, honestly, but the baby seems to like it. 

But, um, anyway... yeah. Those elevated, driven stretches with less sleep have been going on for about eleven months.
When one of those upbeat, energized periods happens, how many days does it usually last at a time?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I've never actually counted the exact number of days. Which is kind of ironic, because I track everyone else's days for a living. My whole life is Microsoft Outlook. I have this incredibly elaborate color-coding system for my boss's calendar. Purple is for external clients, green is for internal check-ins. He tried to get me to change internal to blue once, but blue is already for board meetings. You can't just change a system once it's established, you know? It throws everything out of whack. 

It’s like when the grocery store reorganizes the aisles. I went in for coffee last week and they had moved the entire breakfast section to where the baking supplies used to be. I spent twenty minutes looking for flour before I realized they put it next to the canned soup. Who puts flour next to soup? It makes absolutely zero sense. I ended up just buying a muffin at the bakery instead. They have these really good blueberry muffins with the big sugar crystals on top... 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, how long the upbeat stretches last. Yeah, I really don't know exactly. The days just kind of blur together when I'm feeling like that, so I haven't really kept track.

I actually used to play the saxophone in middle school. The alto sax. I wasn't very good, though. My reed kept squeaking, and my band teacher, Mr. Henderson, he had this comb-over that would flap when he got mad... 

But, uh, yeah. It started about fifteen months ago when I had to start managing everything for my brother.
During those times when you felt unusually upbeat and driven, did it ever cause major problems in your life, lead to trouble at work, or require a hospital stay?

Well, major problems... no, no hospital stays or anything like that. My work has stayed intact overall. Though, I have missed some calendar details, which is so unlike me. I've had to double-check tasks that used to be automatic. Like, I almost booked my boss on a flight to Newark instead of JFK last month. And he hates Newark. He says the lounge there has terrible coffee. Which, speaking of coffee, I finally tried that new espresso place downtown. The one with the exposed brick and the Edison bulbs? It's so cliché, but their cortado is actually fantastic. The barista has this intricate mustache, like a 19th-century bartender. I always wonder how much wax that takes to maintain. It must be exhausting to wake up and sculpt your facial hair every single morning. I usually just shave every three days and call it good. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, work. Yeah, work is mostly fine, just double-checking things. But I have pulled back from other stuff. I used to do these weekend photography outings, you know, nature shots, urban decay, that sort of thing. And I was mentoring a junior admin, too. But I've stepped back from all that because I just don't feel as present or reliable lately.
